facts.text: An electronic control unit (ECU) is a small, rugged computer built into a machine to run a particular job, such as controlling the engine, brakes or collision system.
facts.quote: An electronic control unit is one of the small, rugged computers built into a machine, each running one job such as controlling the engine, the brakes or, here, the collision system.

facts.text: A collision system uses its own ECU or shares an ECU that receives sensor data, runs perception and decision software, and sends a brake request to the brake controller.
facts.quote: The collision system has its own ECU, or shares one, which receives sensor data, runs the perception and decision software, and sends a brake request to the brake controller.

facts.text: ECUs run fixed software, called firmware, on a strict schedule and must respond within guaranteed times.
facts.quote: ECUs run fixed software (firmware) on a strict schedule and must respond within guaranteed times.

facts.text: Hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) benches test a real ECU with its real inputs, outputs and production software against a real-time simulator to prove timing, communications, diagnostics and fail-to-safe behavior.
facts.quote: Hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) benches put the real ECU with its real inputs, outputs and production software in front of a real-time simulator; they prove its timing, communications, diagnostics and fail-to-safe behavior

facts.text: Under one mining regime, ECU HIL testing checks that a disconnection is detected within 500 ms and the machine replies within 50 ms.
facts.quote: for example that a disconnection is detected within 500 ms and the machine replies within 50 ms under one mining regime [Chapter 7]

facts.text: ECU HIL benches cannot prove the sensor front end because test data are injected downstream of the lens or antenna.
facts.quote: What they cannot prove is the sensor front end, because data are injected downstream of the lens or antenna [Chapter 7].

facts.text: ECU scheduling can make a braking function fail even when every sensor value looks realistic.
facts.quote: ECU scheduling is one of the timing effects that can make a braking function fail even when every sensor value looks realistic [Chapter 6]

facts.text: A renderer that is accurate offline may not meet ECU timing deterministically.
facts.quote: a renderer accurate offline may not meet the ECU's timing deterministically [Chapter 11].

facts.text: Every log should include ECU and sensor firmware versions.
facts.quote: ECU and sensor firmware versions belong in every log

facts.text: Controller timing and interfaces still changing in 2027 without impact analysis are an early warning sign for the collision mitigation program.
facts.quote: controller timing and interfaces still changing in 2027 without impact analysis is an early warning sign [Chapters 7, 13].

facts.text: The brake request from the collision ECU to the machine turns a perception decision into a safety action, so its timing and fault behavior need evidence separate from sensor realism.
facts.quote: The brake request from the collision ECU to the machine is where a perception decision becomes a safety action, so its timing and fault behavior need their own evidence, separate from sensor realism [Chapter 7].
